summary.text: Take the counterexample \(n=8=2^3\), for which \(\Omega(8)=3\).  In the Möbius sum, \(\mu(8)=\mu(4)=0\), \(\mu(2)=-1\), and \(\mu(1)=1\), so \(a(8)=8!(H_8-H_4)=25584>0\), contradicting the predicted negative sign.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
H_m=\sum_{j=1}^m \frac1j
\]
be the \(m\)-th harmonic number, and let \(\mu\) denote the Möbius function. The factorial-scaled Möbius transform in the conjecture is
\[
a(n)=n!\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(n/d)H_d
\]
for positive integers \(n\). Also, \(\Omega(n)\) is the number of prime factors of \(n\), counted with multiplicity. The conjecture asserts, for every positive integer \(n\), the equivalence
\[
a(n)<0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\bigl(\Omega(n)\text{ is odd and }\Omega(n)\ge 3\bigr).
\]

We disprove this universal assertion by taking \(n=8\).

The positive divisors of \(8\) are
\[
1,2,4,8.
\]
For these divisors, the arguments \(8/d\) of the Möbius function are respectively \(8,4,2,1\). Recall that \(\mu(1)=1\), that \(\mu(p)=-1\) for a prime \(p\), and that \(\mu(m)=0\) whenever \(m\) is divisible by the square of a prime. Consequently,
\[
\mu(8)=0,\qquad \mu(4)=0,\qquad \mu(2)=-1,\qquad \mu(1)=1.
\]
Substitution into the divisor sum therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{d\mid 8}\mu(8/d)H_d
&=\mu(8)H_1+\mu(4)H_2+\mu(2)H_4+\mu(1)H_8\\
&=0\cdot H_1+0\cdot H_2-H_4+H_8\\
&=H_8-H_4.
\end{aligned}
\]
The difference consists precisely of the last four terms of \(H_8\):
\[
H_8-H_4=\frac15+\frac16+\frac17+\frac18.
\]
Using the common denominator \(840\), this is
\[
\frac{168+140+120+105}{840}=\frac{533}{840}.
\]
Since \(8!=40320=48\cdot840\), it follows that
\[
a(8)=8!\left(H_8-H_4\right)
=40320\cdot\frac{533}{840}
=48\cdot533
=25584.
\]
In particular, \(a(8)>0\), so the assertion \(a(8)<0\) is false.

On the other hand,
\[
8=2^3.
\]
Because \(2\) is prime, this factorization contains exactly three prime factors when multiplicity is counted. Hence
\[
\Omega(8)=3.
\]
The number \(3\) is odd and is at least \(3\). Thus the right-hand side of the conjectured equivalence is true at \(n=8\), whereas the left-hand side is false.

Therefore the claimed equivalence fails for the positive integer \(8\), and the conjecture is false.
